subject: general
question: ________ is a type of water storage system found in Madhya Pradesh.
solution:
The correct answer is **Bonded.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bonded**

 
 
• **Bonded water storage **systems are common in **Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• ​These tank containers, also known as water tank bund, are typically made of **UV-stabilized polyethene **and serve as a protective cover for a liquid tank.
 
• The idea behind this container is that the water that escapes will be contained within the** outer skin** rather than spilling onto the surrounding area in the event that the tank splits or overfills with water.
 
• If the water contains** harmful bacteria**, there may be a risk of contamination spreading, which could lead to cleanup costs or liability for general** health risks.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tunnel**

 
 
• ​Design for tunnels and underground roads is done in **reservoirs**, not every day like it is for other structures. Rock or soil could be used to construct it.
 
• For instance, a **highway** tunnel is designed to withstand external loads imposed by the** rock cover** or any other overburdened material.
 
• Tunnels that carry water, on the other hand, are built to withstand both** permanent and external loads**.
 
 
 
• **Kulh**
 
 
• ​Over four hundred years ago, a local system of canal irrigation known as Kulhs was developed in parts of** Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• The water that was flowing in the streams was diverted into** man-made channels,** which carried the water to a number of villages further down the hillside.
 
• All of the villages came to an agreement on how to manage the water in these kulhs.​
